scenes.text: Imagine being the only tree for two hundred and fifty miles in every direction, and someone still manages to run you over with a vehicle.
This actually happened in 1973 to the Tree of Ténéré, an ancient, sacred acacia that was the sole living thing surviving in a vast, empty stretch of the Sahara Desert.

Nomads used it as a vital landmark for navigation, making it absolutely mind-boggling when a drunk truck driver lost his way and crashed directly into the only obstacle in a hundred thousand square miles.
Today, only a metal sculpture marks where the world's loneliest tree once stood, so do you think this was cursed luck or destiny? Comment below and hit follow for more crazy stories!
